review_conclusions: Every table is contiguous, disjoint, eight-byte aligned at its start, and contained in the declared two-MiB workspace.
Call graph uses 256-byte rows, scans 256 columns, and clears 67584 bytes covering all 65536 edge bytes and 2048 readiness bytes before admission.
Both function-count/header 64 and function-ordinal/header 72 are widened to state_get32/state_put32 after the original byte optimization; header full-word clearing preserves high-zero invariants.

Remaining 128 literals denote x86 ModR/M encoding, ASCII boundary, and the intentionally unchanged 128-byte identifier ceiling. Remaining 1 MiB literals constrain source and output; no old 1536, 17408, 12000 capacity literal remains in reconstructed adapted authoring.
Per-function resource queue capacity 256 remains appropriate because each unique block is queued at most once and per-function blocks remain limited to 256.

Relocation records are guarded before writes. Each operation contributes at most one relative record, each block at most two edge records, each function at most one entry jump, wrapper/export count at most F, plus two optional shared-destructor allocator records.
The relocation-table endpoint 1283072 equals the call-graph start; the conservative 13826-record bound fits 14336 slots with 510 spare.
Canonical Core byte bound 8127488 remains within the unchanged 8 MiB gate. Source, output, per-function blocks, SSA, parameter and instruction limits are unchanged.

Build recipe pins source/predecessor/final artifacts, uses HIA for native compilation and packing with empty PATH, requires a new output directory, checks all four image/executable generations and successor-rebuilt packer, and repeats source/predecessor identity checks at completion.
Compiler packer alone changes private workspace allocation; ordinary application wrapper Core bodies retain their original bytes. No packaging or reproducibility blocker identified.
